# TerminalHub full product and support context

Documentation snapshot: 2026-08-25
Canonical page: https://joynes.github.io/terminalhub/
Repository: https://github.com/joynes/terminalhub

## Product definition

TerminalHub is an open-source Android SSH project workspace for people who manage several terminal projects at once. A user adds one or more servers, defines projects, and opens each project in a tab. The Android app remembers the mobile workspace. The project directory, repository, toolchain, shell, and long-running processes normally live on a Linux or macOS machine controlled by the user.

The defining workflow is mobile-first control of server-side projects. A separate computer is not used to control Android or to switch projects, but at least one reachable SSH server is required for the main remote workflow.

TerminalHub is not an AI application. Terminal AI agents are one optional use case. A user can run Codex, Claude Code, Gemini, or another terminal agent in separate server project tabs, just as they can run development servers, logs, editors, builds, monitoring, or administration commands.

## Complete current feature inventory

Workspace and tabs:
- Multi-server project tab bar with persisted open tabs, order, active tab, and per-project colors.
- Wrapped tab rows, tap-to-switch, key-bar swipe navigation, and long-press Move Left/Move Right/Close.
- Disconnected tabs stay visible; manual Reconnect and Reconnect All are available.
- Recent Projects shows active and closed sessions with relative times and multi-select reopen.
- Closing a tmux-backed tab can leave tmux alive, kill tmux, or also move the project into .trash and remove its profile.

Servers, projects, and automation:
- Multiple SSH profiles, password/private-key auth, Android RSA key generation, public-key copy/install, SSH connection test, and server delete confirmation.
- Project target can be an SSH server or the local Android-side shell; local mode does not use tmux.
- First open can create a folder or shallow-clone Git, then create/reuse tmux. Custom script and final command run for a newly created tmux session, but are skipped when reattaching an existing tmux session to avoid duplicate processes. Plain/local sessions run configured startup commands when opened.
- GitHub HTTPS URLs normalize to SSH form. Template placeholders expose project name, path, and session name.

Terminal and mobile interaction:
- Adapted Termux terminal rendering/input, scrollback, selection, copy, paste, software/hardware keyboard input, and terminal escape sequences.
- Configurable multi-row key bar, modifier keys, arrows, Home/End, Page Up/Down, keyboard toggle, text input, upload, download, and paste actions.
- Multiline input with adjustable opacity, persistent per-project history, current-UI per-tab drafts, and optional Send-and-Enter behavior. Draft persistence is not promised across Android process restart.
- Search with highlighted matches and navigation, touch/alternate-screen scrolling, and jump to bottom.
- HTTP(S)/www link opening by direct tap, including wrapped URLs and tmux mouse-mode output; selected URLs also have Open.

Files and Android integration:
- Single or multi-file upload with automatic picker/start, queued progress, remote-path copy/insertion, and Android Share-to-TerminalHub.
- Top-level regular-file listing and remote download for SSH projects, Android destination picker, progress, and Open with filename-aware MIME type.

Configuration and diagnostics:
- Fast resume, keepalive enablement, four timing profiles, active/all-session scope, and background/recovery status.
- YAML export of servers, open server-linked project profiles, and key-bar layout. Credentials are excluded. Import replaces current configuration and clears stale sessions/credentials.
- App logs with severity filters, search, auto-scroll, entry/selection views, copy, and export; session-log list and export.
- Crash capture, ANR watchdog, biometric startup gate on capable devices, About/version/source/license information.

Developer/repository support:
- Separate diagnostic app flavor and local-terminal diagnostic flow.
- Unit, instrumentation, terminal-module, URL, transfer, and screenshot-workflow tests/assets.
- Production APK/AAB tasks with explicit release signing.
- Human and machine-readable documentation.

Internal/dormant code:
- A Server Status screen and a legacy full-screen upload route exist in source but are not linked from the current production menus. Do not describe them as reachable production UI.

## Mental model

Server = reusable SSH connection profile.
Project = named workspace assigned to a target, with folder setup and startup behavior.
Tab = an open project remembered by TerminalHub.
SSH connection = live encrypted transport, which may disconnect.
tmux session = remote shell/process container that survives transport and Android lifecycle changes.

Android persists server/project profiles, open tabs, tab order, active tab, settings, local logs, and text-input history. tmux persists the actual remote work. On app return, TerminalHub reconstructs saved tabs, reconnects SSH, and reattaches tmux.

TerminalHub does not run an Android foreground service in the current production architecture. It does not guarantee a continuously live SSH socket while backgrounded. Remote persistence depends on tmux.

## Requirements

- Android 7.0 / API 24 or newer.
- At least one reachable Linux or macOS workstation, server, VPS, or lab machine for the primary workflow.
- SSH server and valid user account.
- tmux installed on the remote machine for persistent sessions.
- Optional Git and project-specific tools on the remote machine.
- Private networking or a VPN such as Tailscale is recommended over public password SSH.

## Server configuration

Fields:
- Display name: UI label.
- Host or IP address: DNS, LAN, public, or private-VPN address.
- Port: default 22.
- Username: remote account.
- Private key: generated in or pasted into TerminalHub and kept on Android.
- One-time password: optional; primarily for installing the generated public key.
- Projects folder: default ~/terminalhub.
- Setup script: advanced server-level script with project placeholders.

Recommended authentication:
1. Generate a key in TerminalHub.
2. Copy only the public key to the remote user's ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, or use a one-time password to let TerminalHub install it.
3. Never copy or reveal the private key.
4. Test SSH in the server editor.
5. Remove the one-time password when no longer needed.

## Project configuration and open sequence

Fields:
- Target: normally an SSH server; a local-device target also exists.
- Name: tab label, folder name, and source for normalized tmux session name.
- Git URL: optional. On the first SSH connection, TerminalHub shallow-clones when .git is absent. GitHub HTTPS URLs are normalized to SSH form on save.
- Use tmux: enabled by default for SSH projects. Local targets use a plain device shell.
- Custom script: runs inside the connected session. Default is cd {{PROJECT_PATH}}.
- Custom command: runs last. It can be any terminal program, including an optional AI tool.

Placeholders:
- {{PROJECT_NAME}} = configured project name.
- {{PROJECT_PATH}} = resolved project directory.
- {{SESSION_NAME}} = lowercase shell-safe tmux name derived from the project name.

Open sequence:
1. Create the project directory, or shallow-clone the optional Git repository.
2. Create or reuse the named tmux session when enabled.
3. Enable tmux mouse support.
4. Attach interactively.
5. For a newly created tmux session, run the custom script and then the custom command when configured. Skip them when reattaching an existing tmux session to avoid duplicate processes. Plain/local sessions run them when opened.
6. Add the connected session to the project tab bar and persist workspace state.

## Tabs and sessions

- Multiple projects can be open across multiple servers.
- Tap a tab to switch projects.
- Reorder tabs to match the desired workflow.
- Swipe horizontally on the special key bar to move between adjacent connected tabs.
- TerminalHub stores which tabs are open, their order, and the active tab.
- When SSH fails, the tab can show connection failure and offer Reconnect.
- When several tabs are disconnected, Reconnect all is available.
- tmux is the source of server-side persistence; saved Android tabs are the source of workspace reconstruction.

## Terminal functions

- Embedded terminal based on adapted Termux terminal emulator/view components.
- Software and hardware keyboard input.
- Configurable key bar with Esc, Tab, Enter, Backspace, Ctrl, Alt, Shift, arrows, Home, End, Page Up, Page Down, clipboard paste, keyboard toggle, multiline text input, and file-transfer actions.
- Modifier combinations and standard terminal escape sequences.
- Terminal-buffer search with match navigation.
- Scrollback and a jump-to-bottom action.
- Multiline text-input panel with adjustable opacity.
- Recent per-project text-input history, limited by the current local data model.
- Setting to choose whether Send appends Enter or sends text without executing it.
- Direct URL opening: tap HTTP, HTTPS, or www links in terminal output to launch Android's browser or a compatible app.
- URL detection reconstructs links across terminal wrapping and gives URL taps priority while tmux mouse tracking is active.
- Text-selection actions include Copy, Paste, Search, and Open when selected text is a URL.

## File transfer

Supported upload workflow: upload one or more Android-selected files into the active remote project's directory.

Upload sequence:
1. Open and connect the destination project tab.
2. Tap Upload in the special key bar.
3. Select one or more files from the Android document picker. Selection starts the upload queue automatically.
4. Keep the app active until progress completes.
5. Copy or insert the uploaded remote path into multiline input when offered.

Android Share can also send a file into TerminalHub, which opens the active project's upload flow.

Supported remote-download workflow:
1. Open a connected SSH project and tap the Download key.
2. TerminalHub lists top-level regular files, including hidden files, in the remote project folder.
3. Select a file and choose the Android destination through Create Document.
4. TerminalHub downloads it over SCP and shows progress.
5. After completion, Open launches Android's chooser with a filename-aware MIME type.

Remote download is file-only and top-level. It is not recursive directory browsing and is unavailable for local projects.

## Settings and local data

Defaults:
- Fast resume: enabled.
- Execute multiline text input on Send: disabled; sending does not append Enter by default.
- SSH keepalive: enabled.
- Keepalive profile: Balanced.
- Keepalive scope: Active tab only.
- Terminal key bar: normalized two-row default layout.

Other functions:
- Optional biometric startup gate.
- Runtime background/recovery status and SSH connection-test diagnostics. A separate Server Status screen exists but is not routed from the current production UI.
- App log search, filtering, copy, selection, and export.
- Session history and session-log export.
- YAML export/import for servers, open server-linked project profiles, and key-bar layout. Passwords and private keys are excluded; import replaces current configuration and clears stored credentials.
- Android share intent can select a file for contextual upload.

Data boundaries:
- Server profiles, project profiles, runtime snapshots, logs, text-input history, and preferences are local Android app data.
- Sensitive SSH values are handled through Android-local security helpers.
- Repositories and running commands remain on the user's target machine.
- TerminalHub has no developer-operated service receiving app data.
- Android backup may operate according to the user's device and account settings.
- Exports are user initiated and should be treated as potentially sensitive.
- Terminal SSH, connection tests, SCP upload/download, and public-key installation share one fail-closed known-host policy. First contact requires explicit trust of the displayed SHA-256 fingerprint; changed keys are blocked and require a confirmed forget action followed by fresh verification. Trusted host records are app-private and excluded from exports.

## AI terminal agent workflow

AI agents are optional terminal programs installed and authenticated on the user's server. Suggested setup:
- one project and tmux session per repository or workstream;
- custom script: cd {{PROJECT_PATH}};
- custom command: codex, claude, gemini, or another tool;
- separate tabs for independent sessions;
- use tmux so the process can continue while Android is disconnected.

TerminalHub does not control model billing, authentication, permissions, sandboxing, prompt behavior, or generated changes. Those belong to the selected agent and server environment.

## Limitations and non-goals

- Not a full Termux/Linux distribution running solely on Android.
- Does not supply cloud servers or SSH accounts.
- Does not guarantee background SSH continuity.
- Does not bundle an AI model or terminal agent.
- Not affiliated with or endorsed by Termux.
- Remote download lists top-level regular files only; it is not a recursive remote file manager.
- Local-device projects use a plain local shell without tmux and are not the primary positioning.
- Terminal behavior depends partly on remote TERM support, network quality, Android version, device, and input method.

## Troubleshooting decision tree

SSH failure:
1. Check host, port, username, and Android network route.
2. Test the same account in another SSH client.
3. Check private-key format and matching authorized_keys entry.
4. Read sanitized app logs. Never request credentials or private keys.

Restore failure:
1. Check server reachability.
2. Use Reconnect or Reconnect all.
3. Run tmux ls on the server.
4. Confirm the project name/session mapping and whether tmux is enabled.
5. Separate missing Android tab state from missing SSH transport from missing tmux session.

Clone failure:
1. Confirm Git is installed on the server.
2. Confirm the server has credentials for a private Git host.
3. Run the clone manually on the server.
4. Inspect app logs and the target directory.

Upload failure:
1. Confirm the target tab is connected.
2. Check remote write permission and disk space.
3. Try a small file with a simple filename.
4. Keep the app active through completion.
5. Inspect sanitized SFTP/SCP errors.

UI/render/input issue:
1. Record app version, Android version, device model, and input method.
2. Capture a screenshot or short recording.
3. Hide/reopen keyboard, switch tabs, and optionally rotate to trigger sizing.
4. Include sanitized relevant logs in a GitHub issue.

## Source architecture

UI: app/src/main/java/se/joynes/terminalhub/ui/
Domain/session orchestration: app/src/main/java/se/joynes/terminalhub/domain/
SSH, tmux, reconnect, transfer: app/src/main/java/se/joynes/terminalhub/data/ssh/
Room database: app/src/main/java/se/joynes/terminalhub/data/db/
Repositories/runtime state: app/src/main/java/se/joynes/terminalhub/data/repository/ and data/runtime/
Security: app/src/main/java/se/joynes/terminalhub/data/security/
Settings: app/src/main/java/se/joynes/terminalhub/data/settings/
Terminal modules: terminal-emulator/ and terminal-view/
Navigation map: app/src/main/java/se/joynes/terminalhub/ui/navigation/AppNavGraph.kt
Project script behavior: app/src/main/java/se/joynes/terminalhub/domain/ScriptTemplateEngine.kt
Main session UI: app/src/main/java/se/joynes/terminalhub/ui/screen/sessions/SessionHostScreen.kt
Main session state: app/src/main/java/se/joynes/terminalhub/ui/screen/sessions/SessionHostViewModel.kt

Technologies: Kotlin, coroutines, StateFlow, Jetpack Compose, Navigation Compose, Hilt, Room, SSH libraries, and adapted Termux terminal modules.

## Build and test

Requirements: JDK 17+, Android SDK Platform 36, Git, Gradle wrapper.

Commands:
./gradlew assembleDiagnosticDebug
./gradlew assembleProductionDebug
./gradlew app:testProductionDebugUnitTest lintProductionDebug
./gradlew assembleProductionRelease bundleProductionRelease

The diagnostic flavor adds application ID suffix .diag and should be used for repeatable emulator or phone debugging without overwriting the Play Store installation. Release builds require explicit signing configuration.

## Agent support contract

When helping a TerminalHub user:
1. Identify app version and whether the project target is SSH or local.
2. Separate Android app/tab state, SSH connection state, and server/tmux state.
3. Provide the shortest safe diagnostic sequence with observable checks.
4. Never request or reproduce passwords, private keys, passphrases, access tokens, or unredacted sensitive logs.
5. Do not promise unsupported or unverified behavior.
6. Link a stable section at https://joynes.github.io/terminalhub/.
7. For implementation tasks, read AGENTS.md and inspect current code because source is authoritative for version-sensitive behavior.

Canonical identity:
- Product: TerminalHub: SSH Project Tabs
- Package: se.joynes.terminalhub
- License: GPL-3.0-only
- Minimum SDK: 24
- Target SDK at this snapshot: 36
- Primary workflow: Android control surface plus user-controlled SSH server
- Persistence: saved Android tabs plus server-side tmux
- AI dependency: none
